dedupe_keys.name: swan simulating waves nearshore third generation wave model

description: SWAN is a third-generation spectral wave model that computes random, short-crested wind-generated waves in coastal regions and inland waters. Delft University of Technology develops it, with past support from the US Office of Naval Research and current partial support from Rijkswaterstaat. It represents wave generation, propagation, breaking and dissipation, including dissipation by vegetation, which lets engineers model how salt marshes and mangroves in front of dikes damp waves. It runs on common operating systems with implementation and user manuals, a known bugs and patches list, mailing lists and a tracker. Coverage is any coast or lake with bathymetry and forcing. Format and access: source code and setup wizards from the SWAN website and SourceForge, both of which block the cloud with a browser check, so they were not read. Licence: GNU General Public License, with a request to reference the origin; free. Caveats: it is a phase-averaged model, so it does not resolve diffraction or wave overtopping in detail. It supports design and hazard exposure studies of coastal defences, including hybrid green-grey defences. Related catalogue records are the global mangrove hybrid defence study and the Global Value of Mangroves.
